title: Stakeholder micro-scripts and tech storyboard for private deployments
body:
Purpose
---
This is a compact, execution-focused playbook for sales, solutions, and product partners to use when positioning Redwood's Private (VPC/on-prem) offering to regulated buyers. The goal is short, repeatable micro-scripts per stakeholder plus a technical storyboard that explains control plane vs data plane in plain language and the fallback/incident narratives buyers ask for.

Audience
---
- Solutions engineers and AE SDRs for mid-enterprise and enterprise deals
- Product marketing and field enablement
- Customer success for onboarding and early-run books

Core framing (one-liners to start conversations)
---
- For the security-first buyer: "We can run the inference control plane where you want it—either in your VPC or on your hardware—while keeping model routing, telemetry, and orchestration in a manner you control and audit."
- For the infra buyer: "You keep your keys, your network, and your audit trails. Redwood brings a tuned inference runtime and operational tooling that plugs into your control plane."
- For procurement/legal: "Private deployment is a licensing + support package with a clear upgrade and patch cadence defined in the SLA; cost structure aligns to capacity commits and optional managed services."

Plain-language control plane vs data plane storyboard (short)
---
- Control plane = orchestration, routing rules, rollouts, telemetry collection. Think: who decides model versions, traffic policies, and where we surface alerts.
- Data plane = where inference runs and where request data (prompt, response) touches compute.
- Our recommended deployment: customer-managed control plane inside their VPC (API endpoints, RBAC, KMS integration) + data plane colocated on customer GPUs or in customer VPC subnets.
- Fallback model variants: When capacity is constrained, routing policies can degrade to smaller quantized models that are still pinned to the customer tenancy—no external tenant mixing.

Common buyer objections + tested micro-responses
---
1) "How do you prevent telemetry/metadata exfiltration?"
- Micro-script: "We ship the control plane components as customer-managed services; telemetry is either written to your internal observability backends or encrypted and stored on your S3/R2 with customer keys. No telemetry leaves your network without an explicit opt-in."

2) "We can't allow third-party control planes touching secrets."
- Micro-script: "You retain KMS keys and HSM access. Our control plane does not hold master keys—only short-lived signing tokens that your KMS issues. We also support an air-gapped bootstrap flow for initial install and upgrades."

3) "What about patching and security updates?"
- Micro-script: "We provide a signed patch bundle and a 'maintenance window' playbook; you can choose automated or manual install. For high-compliance customers we offer concierge/managed patching under an enterprise support add-on."

4) "How do we prove data residency and sovereignty?"
- Micro-script: "All inference compute is scheduled in your VPC/subnet and logs are written to your object store under your account. We include an audit report template showing timestamps, host IDs, and which model binary was used for each request."

5) "Vendor lock-in concerns."
- Micro-script: "We use standard container images, documented APIs, and exportable KV/cache formats so you can snapshot and migrate workloads. The control plane communicates over gRPC/HTTPS and we provide a migration checklist for the top three pieces: model artifacts, routing config, and runtime metrics."

Stakeholder-specific micro-scripts (bite-sized)
---
- CISO: "We run the control plane in your VPC, KMS approves keys, and audit logs are retained in your archive for whatever retention you need. We can provide an architecture diagram and risk annex for your audit committee."
- CTO/VP Eng: "You get a production-grade runtime with tuning profiles for latency/cost. We’ll co-design autoscaling policies and give you per-route SLOs and fallback rules so customers never see hard failures during upgrades."
- Infra Lead/Cloud Ops: "Install is Terraform-first, runtime is containerized, and we provide a canary pipeline for upgrades. We’ll hand over Prometheus/OTel exporters and a runbook for node replacement."
- Procurement: "Pricing is split into a platform license + optional managed ops. SLAs cover availability of orchestration services and a defined RTO/RPO for control-plane incidents."
- Legal/Privacy Officer: "We’ll add specific clauses for data processing, subcontractor flows, and breach notification cadence. Template addendum available for DPA and SOC2 scoping."

Competitive differentiation bullets tailored for field use
---
- Compared to cloud-managed APIs: Stronger isolation and auditability with similar developer ergonomics and optional managed upgrades.
- Compared to DIY self-hosted: Shorter time-to-prod, tuned runtime, and professional support for edge cases (KV cache warmup, batching patterns).
- Compared to inference vendors that keep control planes centrally hosted: Transparent routing and cryptographic guarantees around telemetry and key control.

Quick risk heatmap (one-liner per risk + mitigation)
---
- Data leakage via misconfigured S3 buckets -> Mitigation: Default deny policies + pre-flight configuration checks in our installer.
- Slow patch adoption -> Mitigation: Signed patch bundles, optional managed patching.
- Hidden egress costs -> Mitigation: Estimation tool + telemetry showing per-route egress and compute split.
- Performance variability on customer infra -> Mitigation: Benchmark harness + recommended instance/driver matrix and reference configs.

Rollout checklist for Solutions + AE (7 items)
---
1) Confirm legal/regulatory gatekeepers and required contract addenda.
2) Run a short infra discovery call: VPC connectivity, KMS, subnets, CIDR, egress rules.
3) Share architecture diagram and one-page risk annex.
4) Offer a 2-week proof-of-concept with constrained scope (1 model, 1 route, synthetic traffic).
5) Validate telemetry and audit log ingestion to customer stores.
6) Define maintenance windows and emergency rollback criteria.
7) Deliver a short runbook and knowledge-transfer session to on-call rota.

Short sample email snippets (copyable)
---
- To CISO: "Hi — we recommend a control-plane-in-VPC deployment so all audit trails and key handles remain on your account. Attached is a 1-page risk annex and an architecture overview for your review."
- To Infra Lead: "Quick ask: can you confirm if we can open gRPC/443 between the management subnet and runtime subnet and provide a temporary service account for our POC? We’ll supply Terraform modules for install."

Open questions and product asks (internal)
---
- Need a canned architecture diagram variant for air-gapped installs with explicit HSM flows.
- Small feature ask: ability to toggle telemetry export destinations at runtime without control-plane restart.
- Add an exportable audit CSV that matches common audit committee templates (timestamp, user, action, model-id, request-hash).

Appendix: example audit narrative for buyers
---
- "During the POC, all requests were routed through the customer's VPC and written to their S3 bucket. We delivered a signed monthly audit that includes model hashes, node IDs, and request counts. The customer retains the only copy of the master KMS key; Redwood stores no permanent secrets."

Notes for field enablement sessions
---
- Run 30-min roleplay drills with AE + SE where AE runs the first 90s elevator and SE handles the technical deep-dive.
- Capture three objection variants per account and store in CRM under "private-deployments:objections".

End of doc.
